page: Microsoft Azure L2aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an x86_64 AMD processor. The configuration includes 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance provides 1440 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, contains no GPU accelerators, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The primary architectural distinction of this instance is the high ratio of local NVMe SSD capacity paired with a small compute profile. With 1440 GB of local high-speed disk attached to 2 vCPUs, the virtual machine delivers substantial local storage density. This design provides qualitative cost efficiency for organizations that require local fast-access storage without paying for unneeded vCPUs, avoiding the overhead of external disk services for temporary or replica operations.

A notable tradeoff is the low CPU core count, which limits parallel computing capabilities and high-throughput application serving. The instance is suited for localized relational and non-relational database nodes, distributed caching layers, log indexing services, ETL processing pipelines, and data stores with heavy local read-write storage demands.
description: Microsoft Azure L2aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for I/O-intensive workloads requiring direct local storage access. Virtualized through Microsoft Hyper-V using an x86_64 AMD processor, the instance supplies 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, equating to 8.0 GB per vCPU. A prominent feature is the inclusion of 1440 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high storage volume alongside a compact compute footprint. The system features no GPUs and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware structure yields high storage-to-core efficiency, though the 2-vCPU configuration limits parallel compute throughput. The server is suited for database servers, key-value caches, log collectors, and data ingest stages needing low-latency NVMe access.
